messages:
amelia: noticed a sharp p95/p99 spike in hosted-us-west-2 starting ~12:05 UTC. p95 ~200ms -> 700ms, p99 ~450ms -> 1.6s. queue depth up on router nodes. any ideas?
raj: saw same in metrics. queue_depth per-host jumped, but CPU/GPU utilization looks steady.
nate: throwing profiler traces now. I suspect kernel selection mispredict with mixed seq lengths — we hit a fallback kernel that serializes batches.
maria: kv-cache eviction rate ticked up too, curious if cache churn is causing extra tail latency.
david: noisy tenant? which customer? I see a tenant with many short completions beginning at spike start.
amelia: tenant id 8732 — mostly short requests, but a few long ones interleaved. could be hetero seqlen pattern.
perf-agent: uploaded sampling profile: `top_time_by_op` shows `attention_kernel_fallback` at 42% of tail time, `serialize_dispatch` 18%, `kv_cache_eviction` 12%.
nate: here's the quick profiler dump I pulled from a fed host (trimmed):
```
# profiler slice
attention_kernel_fast: 38ms
attention_kernel_fallback: 520ms
serialize_dispatch: 220ms
kv_cache_lookup: 34ms
kv_cache_eviction: 86ms
batch_wait: 140ms
```
raj: interesting — fallback kernel is dominating. why did we pick fallback? kernel selection log: `seqlen_percentile: p99=1024, p50=42 => selection: conservative` — heuristics picked a long-friendly kernel. That one is slower for many short requests.
maria: plus kv-cache thrash: the long requests blow cache with large KV windows, evicting prefixes used by short requests -> more recompute. combo is bad.
david: any recent change to kernel heuristics?
amelia: we rolled a heuristics tweak yesterday that biases towards minimizing p99 for long sequences. maybe over-aggressive.
raj: I can reproduce locally with a mixed synthetic workload. if I inject 5% long (1k tokens) and 95% short (<=64) we hit fallback and serialization, p99 jumps.
nate: potential mitigations: 1) conservative short-first routing: if batch composition is >80% short, force short kernel. 2) kv-cache soft-reserve to avoid evicting small-tenants pref. 3) quick rollback of yesterday's heuristic.
sre-oncall: impact: ~3% of hosted customers saw elevated tail, routing fallback happened across 6 router nodes. recommend hotfix?
amelia: agree we should hotfix to roll back heuristic while we implement targeted fixes.
david: can we do a targeted config roll on us-west-2 only?
amelia: yes, schedule a hot rollback for that region. @deploy-bot start canary deploy config: `kernel_heuristic=legacy` to 10% nodes.
deploy-bot: canary started. 10% router nodes in us-west-2 updated. monitoring for p95/p99.
raj: after canary: p95 down ~40%, p99 down ~55% on canary hosts.
amelia: promote to 50% then 100% if trend holds.
deploy-bot: promotion to 50% done. metrics show continued improvement.
perf-agent: I pushed an isolated test harness that reproduces eviction pattern; saving logs to /artifacts/mixed-seqlen-repro-8732.tgz
maria: for medium-term: we should change kernel selection to consider batch composition (fraction short vs long) and add a fast-path pre-check before selecting fallback. also add kv-cache tenant soft-reserve for small-hot tenants.
nate: will open two PRs: `kernel-selection-batch-aware` and `kvcache-soft-reserve`. include perf tests and regression gates.
david: add an eval to Redwood Optimize to flag this mixed workload for automatic recommendation.
amelia: thanks everyone — action items: raj monitor post-deploy, nate + david PRs, maria kvcache proposal, sqs ticket for postmortem.
sre-oncall: creating incident ticket INF-2026-432 and assigning follow-ups.
amelia: closing loop: retro planned tomorrow 10:00am PT. short blameless postmortem after full roll out. :thumbsup:
